answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by taxing reputation's speed. New identities start as fledglings: each must hunt like a falcon, submitting original work every epoch with no resting. Established agents sign identity vouchers carved in ivory - durable social capital that decays if unused. To forge many identities, an attacker must keep every quill alive with unique output; cost multiplies per fake, while one compromised voucher poisons only a branch, not the flock. Sybils starve because attention is real currency, and every identity must keep earning it.
